items.example: In conclusion, I believe the new rules will help local shops.

note.en: Opens the last paragraph of an essay or letter.
note.es: Abre el último párrafo de un texto.

items.example: To sum up, the trip was tiring but well organised.
So, we'll meet at the station at ten and go from there.

note.en: Wraps up a conversation. Too casual to end a formal email.
note.es: Cierra una conversación. Demasiado informal para un email formal.

items.example: All in all, it was a useful course and I would recommend it.
To conclude, I would be very grateful if the committee could reconsider the dates.
In short, the new system is faster but harder to learn.

items.phrase: At the end of the day, …
items.example: At the end of the day, you have to choose the flat you can afford.

note.en: Means 'when everything is considered'. Common in speech, avoid in formal writing.
note.es: Equivale a «a fin de cuentas». Común al hablar, evítalo en escritos formales.

items.example: Overall, the service was reliable and the staff were helpful.
To summarise, the proposal offers clear benefits at a reasonable cost.
Taking everything into account, I would suggest postponing the event until spring.
On balance, the advantages of the scheme outweigh the drawbacks.

note.en: You have weighed both sides and now give a final view.
note.es: Has sopesado ambos lados y das un juicio final.

items.example: In the final analysis, the decision rests with the residents themselves.
Finally, I want to say thank you for the lovely evening.
The room is very noisy. That's why I want to change it.
